data.body:
Correction to this ticket's "Why this matters" section, and the sharper scope it implies.

That section says the gate being red means "no commit's authorship is being verified". That is wrong, and I wrote it before checking how the Verified vote actually consumes this workflow.

`gerrit-verify.yaml` defines its **own** `verify-identity` job — "verify-identity (whole-store authorship gate)", at roughly line 499 — and that job is what `vote.needs` aggregates into the Verified vote. It performs the same whole-store authorship walk and it does **not** contain the pack-size budget. That is why changes have continued to earn `Verified +1` throughout this outage, and it means pre-merge authorship verification has never stopped.

What is actually lost is narrower and still real: the standalone `verify-identity.yml` lane — push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, and the every-6-hours schedule — is the **periodic whole-store sweep**, and it has produced no authorship verdict on any run since 2026-09-15. A change that lands green can still be contradicted later by store-wide state the pre-merge walk did not see; the scheduled sweep is what would catch that, and it has been silent.

The remedy is unchanged, and this correction actually reinforces the chosen approach. Because `verify-identity.yml` is a parity-governed source workflow (`scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` requires every unconditional job in it to be folded into `vote.needs`), splitting the budget into a **second job** would have forced the pack overage into the Verified hot path, where it would have blocked every change. Deferring the verdict **within the single existing job** avoids that entirely. `check_verify_gate_parity.py` reports OK against the implemented change.

Implementation detail worth recording, because it is the part that is easy to get wrong: the pack is measured immediately after checkout and judged in the final step, rather than simply moved to the end. The `Mount tickets branch as a worktree` step fetches the event log into the object database, so a measurement taken after it would be a materially larger quantity than the budget was ever calibrated against. Moving the whole check to the end would have silently changed what is under budget while appearing to preserve it.

Change 2987 implements this. Five structural tests pin the ordering by parsing the workflow rather than observing a CI run, so they hold under any CI provider and under none; four of the five fail against the previous ordering, and the fifth asserts the fail-closed invariant that must hold either way.

Remaining unverified: acceptance criteria 1, 2 and 5 require a run log from this lane, which cannot exist until the change lands. Once it merges I will trigger the lane via `workflow_dispatch` and attach the step conclusions showing the authorship verdict reported alongside a still-failing pack budget.
